name: History and Download History
location: Firefox: %USERPROFILE%\AppData\Roaming\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\<randomtext>.default\places.sqlite (Win7+; XP: %USERPROFILE%\Application Data\...) ; Chrome/Edge: %USERPROFILE%\AppData\Local\Google\Chrome\User Data\<Profile>\History and \Microsoft\Edge\User Data\<Profile>\History (Win7+; XP under Local Settings\Application Data)
purpose: Records websites visited by date and time, forming the primary source for reconstructing a user's browsing activity.
key_fields: Profile identifier — look for multiple Chromium profiles ("Default", "Profile 1", etc.)
normal_baseline: History entries correspond to expected work-related or personal browsing consistent with the user's role, spread across normal business hours.
anomalies: History entries for known malicious-tool distribution sites, paste sites, or C2 infrastructure
A second, unexpected Chromium profile directory (e.g. "Profile 1") with its own separate history, suggesting an attempt to segregate activity from the primary profile
A visit-count spike to a single external domain immediately preceding a security incident
anti_forensic_notes: Web browser artifacts are stored per local user account, so history for one account tells you nothing about another; clearing history removes rows from the SQLite tables but does not necessarily overwrite the underlying database pages, so carving deleted records can sometimes recover cleared history.
interpretation: Always check for multiple profiles in Chromium-based browsers before concluding history is complete — a single "History" file query against the wrong profile folder silently misses activity in another profile. This is the general browsing-history counterpart to the more specific `browser-downloads` (download manager metadata) and `media-history` (audio/video playback) entries.
